name: Viktor Orbán
role: Prime minister of Hungary (1998–2002, 2010–2026); leader of Fidesz
summary: Leader of Fidesz and prime minister of Hungary. His governments have stressed national sovereignty, a family policy built on marriage between a man and a woman and on birth incentives, strict limits on migration, and close economic and diplomatic ties with China and Russia-linked energy projects. In a 2014 speech he described the state he was building as 'illiberal'; scholars describe the resulting system as a hybrid regime.

sources.title: Viktor Orbán (Wikipedia article, full text opened)
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.usedFor: Record of laws and policies (2011 constitution, 2012 flat tax, 2014 Paks II deal, 2020 gender-recognition change, 2021 child-protection law, 2017 attacks on Soros-funded NGOs, status law, kindergarten curriculum, China ties) and a summary of his 2014 Tusnádfürdő speech.

sources.title: Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's speech at the 3rd Budapest Demographic Summit (5 September 2019)
sources.author: Viktor Orbán
sources.usedFor: Full English transcript: migration as a rejected answer to population decline, traditional-family support, child-benefit and employment linkage, national foundations, constitutional protection against EU and international decisions, 'population replacement' remarks.

sources.title: Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's opening speech at the 2nd Budapest World Congress of Families (2017)
sources.author: Viktor Orbán
sources.usedFor: Full English transcript: Europe's population decline, rejection of migration as remedy, family policy, Christianity and Europe, constitutional protection of family policy.

sources.title: Orbán causes outrage for opposing 'mixed race' society in Hungary (Insight Hungary, 28 July 2022)

sources.usedFor: Reported wording of the July 2022 Băile Tușnad remarks on 'mixed race', 'non-Europeans' and migration as 'population exchange'. Secondary reporting; no answer relies on it alone.

Judgment calls: elite-replacement was answered +1 rather than +2 because he speaks of 'political forces' and 'people' rather than elites; discourage-race-mixing and diversity-weakens-cohesion were left null as nearby but not matching; restrict-foreign-funding and party-controls-media were set at +1 low because they rest on contested record evidence.
